title: Premium Account Rules for the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy
content:
These rules govern how a LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy term is billed and how payments, returned payments, refunds and mortgagee changes are recorded on the policy's premium account. The premium balance is the premium and fees owed on the landlord policy: a positive balance is owed to the carrier, a negative balance is a credit.

## Retired clause

The clause "each term is billed on its plan's schedule" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis. The plan schedules below remain the description of each plan.

## Billing plans

| Plan | Installments in the term | Schedule |
|---|---|---|
| Annual | 1 | one installment due on the term effective date |
| Two-pay | 2 | two installments six calendar months apart |
| Quarterly | 4 | four installments three calendar months apart |
| Mortgagee escrow | 1 | one installment to the mortgagee, with a mortgagee invoice of the same amount and due date |

Each later installment is the term premium divided by the installment count, rounded half-up to the cent, and installment 1 takes the difference. Hypothetical example: a quarterly term premium of 1,000.01 USD gives later installments of 250.00 USD each and an installment 1 of 250.01 USD.

Installments are billed only while the policy is bound, in force, pending cancellation or pending nonrenewal, as the policy record shows before the installment is billed.

## Service charges

The following clauses are **no longer in force** and have been superseded by the current basis for each charge: "the installment service charge is charged on each installment after the first"; "a late fee once per installment still unpaid more than the late-fee grace days after its due date"; and "a returned-payment fee once per returned payment".

Still in force: none of the installment, late or returned-payment charges is made on a mortgagee-billed term, and none is made when the tier's amount for it is 0.00.

## Payments, returned payments and refunds

- Payments apply to the oldest charge first and are recorded with their confirmation or check number exactly as issued.
- A returned payment reverses the one payment it references, in full.
- A refund is issued only when the premium balance is a credit of at least the tier's refund minimum, and it goes to the payer of the most recent payment.

## Mortgagee changes

A mortgagee change is recorded only with the mortgagee's name and loan number exactly as they appear on the mortgage statement.

## Basis Q&A

**Can a refund be issued on a credit balance of 3.00 USD?** No; the smallest credit refunded is the tier's refund minimum, 5.00 USD on every tier.

**Who receives a refund?** The payer of the most recent payment, whether the insured or the mortgagee.
